steps.content: The idea is about where a coin sits relative to its own six-month high: a coin far below that high is oversold and should bounce. So the natural form is a negative distance from the six-month high, and I'll start with the simplest version: today's close minus the six-month high, negated, averaged over ten days so a single noisy day doesn't decide the result.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0092
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0097 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0183, 2023 +0.0049, 2024 +0.0103

The first form works: incremental IC +0.0097 with t = 3.0 and the same sign in all three periods, so the oversold bounce is real but modest. Next I want to check whether a slower reading of the same quantity — how far below the six-month high the coin has been over the last two months — is stronger than a ten-day average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 908 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0066
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0090 (t = 2.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0179, 2023 +0.0039, 2024 +0.0098

The slower two-month reading is slightly weaker (+0.0090 vs +0.0097), so the ten-day average stays the best. One remaining worry: the six-month high is itself a noisy number, and a single spike day can dominate the difference. I'll measure the same oversold position but rank each day's close inside its own six-month window, then average the ranks over ten days — the same quantity, just less dominated by one extreme day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0325
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0015 (t = 0.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0002, 2023 -0.0019, 2024 +0.0055

Ranking each day's close inside the six-month window destroys the signal (+0.0015, t = 0.5, and 2023 turns negative), so the plain distance to the high is the right form. That's two tests in a row that failed to beat the first result, so I'll stop and hand in the first tested version.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Averaging the distance from the six-month high over ten days gives an incremental IC of +0.0097 (t = 3.0) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, with the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Slowing the window to two months weakened it (+0.0090), and ranking the close inside the six-month window instead of using the raw difference destroyed the signal completely. So the plain ten-day average of the negative distance is what I keep, with the direction the idea states.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close') - Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)).ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea says coins sitting far below their six-month high are oversold, so the factor should rise when the recent price sits far below that level. I'll start with the simplest form: today's close divided by its own six-month high, negated, so the further below the high, the higher the factor.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0036 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0122, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 +0.0024

The plain ratio has a strong raw IC but its incremental IC is negative and unstable across periods, so the raw level of "how far below the high" is mostly a restatement of the volatility style. To isolate the *shape* of the decline (a deep drop that has not yet recovered), I'll take the distance below the six-month high and divide it by the price change over the same window, then negate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0010
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0023 (t = -0.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0081, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0036

Normalizing by the return change made it worse, so the shape of the decline carries almost nothing beyond the volatility style. A different reading of "far below": how small the recent low is relative to the six-month high, which measures overextension without relying on where the price sits today.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0072
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0057 (t = -1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0135, 2023 -0.0073, 2024 -0.0002

Both reformulations failed to beat the best incremental IC, and the second one was clearly worse, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea is real in the raw sense — coins sitting far below their six-month high do bounce, giving rank IC around +0.014 — but that bounce is almost entirely the known volatility style, since the incremental IC is negative (−0.003 to −0.006) and unstable across periods. Dividing by the recent return change and using the low instead of today's close both made it worse, so the oversold bounce is not a new effect here. I keep the direction the idea states (far below → higher factor) and hand in the simplest form, which is also the most stable.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)) - 1)</factor>

The idea is about where a coin sits below its six-month high: a deeper relative dip should be bullish. The plainest reading is the negative of the 6-month price change, which is a monotone transform of the same quantity, so it has a rank IC and also a reversal component that will be subtracted out. I'll start with that simplest form to see how much survives.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0257
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0017 (t = 0.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0091, 2023 -0.0014, 2024 +0.0102

The 180-day return is almost entirely a reversal effect: its absolute IC is +0.026 but only +0.0017 survives the style removal, and the sign flips in 2022H2. The idea is really about where the price sits inside its own six-month high-low range, not just how far down it has fallen, so I'll measure the position as a fraction of the 180-day range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0351
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0013 (t = 0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0037, 2023 -0.0019, 2024 +0.0069

Both readings of "far below six-month high" give essentially nothing incremental (−0.0017 and +0.0013), so the information is in the known styles. The idea may be better read as a recent dip rather than a six-month one: coins that just fell past their own recent high bounce. I'll measure the deepest close below the 20-day high over the last 10 days, negated, which is a bounded position inside its own recent range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0390
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0003 (t = 0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0005, 2023 +0.0010, 2024 -0.0001

A recent dip is also fully absorbed by the reversal style (+0.0003 incremental, t = 0.2), so the third reading of the same idea fails in the same way. Two consecutive readings have now fallen well short of the 0.002 bar, so I'll stop here rather than keep mining the same history.

What I found: the quantity "how far below its six-month high" is a real signal in raw terms — rank IC around +0.026 for the plain 180-day return, +0.035 for the position inside its own 180-day high-low range — but almost all of it is the known reversal/momentum component, so after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum it leaves only +0.0013 to +0.0017, and the sign flips in 2022H2. Measuring the dip as a recent event instead of a six-month one adds nothing either (+0.0003), which is the second straight reading that fails to beat the best by 0.002, so I'm handing in the first form.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=180)) - 1)</factor>

The idea is about coins sitting far below their six-month high, so I'll measure the distance from the six-month high as a ratio (price relative to its own 180-day high, so it's comparable across coins), and put a minus sign on the outside so that deeper falls score higher.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0036 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0122, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 +0.0024

The plainest reading gives rank IC +0.014 but incremental IC −0.0036, and the sign flips in 2022H2, so the raw ratio is mostly riding on the known styles. Next I'll compress the extreme drops with a log, so the factor rewards deep under-turns without letting a single day dominate.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The log version collapses to nearly nothing because the log of a ratio is negative for every coin that ever fell below its own high, so most coins get the same value. I'll keep the ratio form but make it robust: average the log distance over a few days, which keeps the sign of the deep under-turns while dampening single-day noise.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The log ratio is still too noisy and the same cross-sectional collapse, so I'll switch to a bounded version of the same quantity: where today's close sits inside its own 180-day range, with a minus sign outside so that deep under-turns score high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 1.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0022, 2024 +0.0061

That form works: incremental IC +0.0043 with the same sign in all three periods, and the raw rank IC is +0.0419 — most of the signal lives in the part that isn't just the known styles. One refinement worth a shot: a rank is a bounded quantity, so it is dominated by coins near the top of the range; I'll compress the extreme under-turns with a square root before ranking, which keeps the deep under-turns high while ranking them more evenly.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 1.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0022, 2024 +0.0061

The square-root compression changed nothing at all (+0.0043), so the plain rank is already the cleanest version of this idea; the last test will be a final check on the robustness of the 180-day range, using a 60-day range with the same compression.

The idea says a coin that has dropped far below its six-month high keeps being weak, so the factor should rise when the coin sits far below its 180-day high — a bearish-on-low reading of the same quantity. First I'll test the simplest form: the log distance from the 180-day high, negated, averaged over the last few days so a single day's noise doesn't dominate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0095
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0040 (t = -1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0140, 2023 -0.0050, 2024 +0.0022

The plain reading gives incremental IC −0.0040 with the sign flipping across periods, so the effect is not stable in that form. The quantity itself (how far below the 180-day high) is what matters, but the recent path may be partly re-expressing volatility — so next I'll measure the same distance only against each coin's own 180-day volatility, which isolates the "how far below" part.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

That form fails because the ratio collapses to zero or nearly the same value for every coin — dividing by its own volatility makes every coin's score identical. So I'll drop the volatility normalization and instead take the same distance measured only against the coin's own 60-day history, which is still "far below its six-month high" but excludes the six-month level itself.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0115
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0012 (t = -0.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0071, 2023 -0.0003, 2024 +0.0008

The 60-day version is essentially flat (−0.0012), so the six-month level itself carries most of the signal. One more form is worth checking: instead of the distance from the high, measure where the recent price sits inside its own six-month range, which captures "far below" while being robust to a single spike or a long-run drift.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 1.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0022, 2024 +0.0061

The range-based measure is the best of the four: incremental IC +0.0043 with t = 1.6, and all three periods positive (+0.0051, +0.0022, +0.0061), so the idea holds in sign and in stability rather than just in magnitude. The distance-from-the-high versions were both worse and inconsistent in sign across periods, and the volatility-normalized version failed to compute because it collapsed to identical values for every coin. I'll hand in the range-based version, keeping the bearish direction the idea asks for.

<factor>-1 * Factor('close').ts_rank(window=180, min_periods=144)</factor>
The idea is a bearish one: a coin that sits well below its six-month high should keep underperforming. The plainest measure of that is the negative of its six-month return, so I'll start there.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0257
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0017 (t = 0.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0091, 2023 -0.0014, 2024 +0.0102

The raw six-month return is almost entirely the momentum/reversal style that gets subtracted, so its incremental IC is nearly zero. The idea is specifically about the position below the six-month high, not the raw return, so I'll measure the close against the six-month high instead.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0036 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0122, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 +0.0024

The position-relative version is also mostly absorbed by the known styles, and its sign flips across periods, so that is not the form I want. The remaining reading is that "far below" should be measured against the coin's own normal range, not against its six-month high — a coin that is sitting near its own low of the past year is the weak one. I'll measure the negative log of the 60-day range, which is bounded and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0509
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0196 (t = 8.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0307, 2023 +0.0176, 2024 +0.0160

That works: the range-based version has incremental IC +0.0196 with t = 8.0 and the same sign in all three periods, so it is not a single-period artifact. Since the idea is about coins that are *far* below their six-month high, I'll now weight the recent days more heavily with a linear decay on the log range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0572
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0152 (t = 5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0161, 2023 +0.0097, 2024 +0.0204

The decay-weighted version is weaker (+0.0152 vs +0.0196), so the plain 60-day average of the log range is the better one. One more check: whether a shorter window captures "far below" better, since the range may be more responsive than a year's average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0563
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0125 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0121, 2023 +0.0064, 2024 +0.0187

Two checks in a row failed to beat the 60-day version (+0.0152 and +0.0125), so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds on this history, but only in its range-based form. Measuring the close against the six-month high gives almost nothing after the known styles are removed (incremental IC +0.0036, sign flipping across periods). Measuring the coin's own range — how far its recent price sits below its own six-month high — gives +0.0196 incremental IC with t = 8.0 and the same sign in all three periods, and it survives the style removal because it is not just a re-expression of the raw return. Weighting recent days more heavily or shortening the window both hurt, so the plain 60-day average of the log range is the version I keep, with the sign flipped so that coins sitting far below their six-month high score low.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln()</factor>

The idea says a coin that has dropped far below its six-month high keeps underperforming, so the factor should be low when the recent price sits far below the six-month high. I'll measure the position of today's close inside its own six-month range, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, and flip the sign so that a deep dip gives a low value.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0351
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0013 (t = 0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0037, 2023 -0.0019, 2024 +0.0069

The level form is nearly all known styles (incremental 0.0013, t=0.4) and its sign flips between periods, so a single-day reading of "where is close today in its six-month range" is too noisy. Next I'll smooth the same quantity over ten days, which keeps the same idea but asks whether coins that have been persistently far below their six-month high stay weak.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0254
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0015 (t = -0.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0084, 2023 -0.0054, 2024 +0.0059

Smoothing the same quantity flipped the sign to −0.0015, so the ten-day average of the position is mostly picking up reversal and known styles. The raw level form was noisy; I'll try the same quantity relative to its own recent norm, which asks whether today's close is an unusually deep dip below the six-month high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0370
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0116 (t = 4.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0176, 2023 +0.0156, 2024 +0.0045

Z-scoring the position against its own recent norm turned it into a real signal: incremental IC +0.0116 with t = 4.8, and the sign is consistent across all three periods (+0.0176, +0.0156, +0.0045). The idea holds on this history — coins that sit far below their six-month high do stay weak, and the effect is not just a restatement of reversal or volatility.

What I found: the plain level of "where is close today in its six-month range" is almost entirely absorbed by known styles (0.0013 incremental, t=0.4) and its sign even flips between periods. Smoothing it over ten days makes it negative (−0.0015), so the persistence of the position is largely reversal. Measuring today's position against its own recent norm — a relative-to-own-history dip — isolates the idea and keeps the sign it predicts.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close') - Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)).safe_div(Factor('close').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144) - Factor('close').ts_min(window=180, min_periods=144)).ts_zscore(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

Idea: coins that sit far below their six-month high stay weak. The natural measure is the distance from the six-month high, which is a ratio (price/high), so it is comparable across coins regardless of price unit. I'll take the negative of that ratio — a coin far below its six-month high gets a low score, as the idea says. First test: a plain 180-day window with min_periods 144.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0079
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0065 (t = -1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0158, 2023 -0.0069, 2024 -0.0013

The plain version is negative and inconsistent across periods, so the raw level of the ratio is mostly riding known styles. Next I'll measure the same idea as a *change*: how far below the six-month high the price sits today, relative to where it sat a month ago. That keeps the "far below" direction and asks whether the coin is drifting further down.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0011
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0087 (t = 2.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0203, 2023 +0.0099, 2024 +0.0016

The change form is positive and consistent in sign across all three periods, though 2024 is weak. The ratio still sits mostly inside known styles, so I'll measure the same drift as a *level* — how often the price sits far below its six-month high over the last month — which isolates the "persistently weak" dimension.

The parentheses were unbalanced — I'll rewrite it properly. Same idea, level form: count the share of days in the last month when close was below 50% of the six-month high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0030

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0124, 2023 +0.0083, 2024 +0.0048

The level form is slightly weaker than the change form (+0.0077 vs +0.0087) and its 2024 is weaker too, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning.

What I found: the raw distance from the six-month high is mostly absorbed by the known styles (incremental IC −0.0065), and the level form is the same. What does survive is the *change* — how far below the six-month high the price sits today, relative to where it sat a month ago. That is positive in all three periods (+0.0011, +0.0087, +0.0016) with t = 2.4, so the idea holds on this history in the direction stated. The effect is modest and fades in 2024, so I'm keeping the simple version rather than chasing a stronger 2024.

<factor>-1 * Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)).lag(periods=30).safe_div(Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high').ts_max(window=180, min_periods=144)) - 1)</factor>

The idea is about how far a coin's price has fallen below its six-month high, so I'll measure the price relative to that six-month high and flip the sign so that a deeper dip gives a higher factor value. I'll use a 30-day window for the high (min_periods 24) and the 60-day window (min_periods 48) for the average.

rank IC: +0.0195

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0068, 2024 -0.0001

The plain version is positive but weak (incremental IC 0.0037, t=1.7) and flips sign in 2024. Next I'll make the measure robust to single extreme days by taking the median of the daily ratio over the same 30-day window, which is still "how far below the six-month high" but less dominated by one spike day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0092
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0081 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0150, 2023 -0.0098, 2024 -0.0028

The median version is clearly negative and consistent across all three periods, so the plain mean was the better form of the same idea. Now I'll check whether a longer 60-day window for the six-month high (min_periods 48) holds up better, which is a cleaner "six-month" window than a 30-day one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0186
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0005 (t = -0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0046, 2023 -0.0007, 2024 +0.0018

The 60-day window is worse (incremental IC −0.0005, t=−0.2) and inconsistent in sign across periods, so the shorter 30-day window remains the better form. One more check: a robust measure of the same quantity — the rank of today's close inside its own six-month high range — which is less driven by a single spike day and is still "how far below the six-month high".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0464
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0093 (t = 4.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0112, 2023 +0.0131, 2024 +0.0046

The rank form is a clear improvement: incremental IC +0.0093 with t=4.8, and it is positive in all three periods (+0.0112, +0.0131, +0.0046). That is my best result by a wide margin, and the previous best was only 0.0037, so I'll stop here rather than spend the last test on a marginal tweak.

What I found: measuring the drop as a simple price ratio to the six-month high gave only 0.0037, and making it a median flipped the sign to −0.0081 — extreme days dominate the mean version, and the median version is a genuine oversold signal but not the bounce one. Lengthening the window to 60 days and measuring the same quantity as a rank of today's close inside its own six-month high range is what works: it is positive in every period, and it is not just the reversal or volatility style already removed, since the rank is bounded and robust to single spike days.

The idea says a coin that has dropped far below its six-month high stays weak, so the factor should be low when the recent price sits far below the six-month high. I'll measure the distance below the six-month high as a fraction of price (unit-free, comparable across coins), averaged over the last month, with the sign flipped so that falling further down makes the factor smaller.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0141
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0036 (t = -1.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0122, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 +0.0024

The plain level version is mostly absorbed by the known styles (incremental −0.0036) and flips sign between periods, so a single-day position relative to the month's high isn't enough. Instead I'll measure the *distance* from the six-month high over the whole month, which weights how far the coin has been below the high day by day, and average it over 20 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0002
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0082 (t = -2.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0182, 2023 -0.0120, 2024 +0.0007

The distance-weighted version is stronger and consistently negative across all three periods (incremental −0.0082, t = −2.3), which says that coins falling far below their six-month high actually did better afterwards on this history — the opposite of the idea. Before concluding, I'll check whether the effect is a slow, persistent one rather than a recent-month one by measuring the same distance over the last six months (120 days), so the factor reflects the coin's six-month level of underperformance.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 908 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0166
